name: SIRIUS
intel: Sirius A is the brightest star in the night sky. It is a binary system with a faint white dwarf companion, Sirius B ('The Pup'), which packs the mass of the Sun into the volume of the Earth.

name: CANOPUS
intel: The second brightest star in the sky. It is a supergiant yellow-white star used extensively for spacecraft navigation due to its brightness and location away from the ecliptic plane.

name: RIGEL KENT
intel: Alpha Centauri is the closest star system to the Solar System. It is a triple system consisting of Rigel Kentaurus A, B, and the faint red dwarf Proxima Centauri, which hosts an Earth-sized planet.

name: ARCTURUS
intel: A red giant relatively close to Earth. It has a high proper motion, moving across the sky faster than almost any other first-magnitude star. It likely originated from a dwarf galaxy consumed by the Milky Way.

name: VEGA
intel: Vega was the northern pole star 12,000 years ago and will be again in the future. It rotates so rapidly (236 km/s) that it bulges at the equator, making the poles significantly hotter than the middle.

name: CAPELLA
intel: A unique quadruple system. The primary source is actually two yellow giant stars orbiting each other every 104 days. They are joined by a distant pair of red dwarfs.

name: RIGEL
intel: A massive blue supergiant located at Orion's foot. It is illuminating the nearby Witch Head Nebula. Despite being 800+ light years away, it shines brighter than stars 10x closer.

name: PROCYON
intel: Procyon is just beginning to evolve off the main sequence into a sub-giant. Like Sirius, it hides a tiny White Dwarf companion that was only confirmed telescopically in 1896.

name: BETELGEUSE
intel: A colossal red supergiant nearing the end of its life. If placed in our solar system, its surface would extend past Jupiter. It is a candidate for a Type II supernova in the near astronomical future.

name: ACHERNAR
intel: The least spherical star known. It spins so fast (250 km/s) that its equatorial diameter is 56% larger than its polar diameter, giving it the shape of a flattened M&M candy.

name: HADAR
intel: Beta Centauri is a triple star system. The two main components are massive blue giants orbiting each other every 357 days. It serves as a pointer to the Southern Cross.

name: ALTAIR
intel: Part of the Summer Triangle. Direct imaging has revealed its surface details, showing a distinct dark band of gravity darkening around its equator due to its rapid rotation.

name: ACRUX
intel: The southernmost star of the Southern Cross. It is actually a multiple system; telescopes reveal two blue stars, while a third component is invisible to the eye.

name: ALDEBARAN
intel: The 'Eye of the Bull'. Aldebaran appears to be part of the Hyades cluster, but this is a line-of-sight coincidence; it is actually half the distance of the cluster behind it.

name: SPICA
intel: A rotating ellipsoidal variable. The two stars in this binary system are so close (orbiting every 4 days) that tidal forces distort them into egg shapes, causing brightness variations.

name: ANTARES
intel: The 'Rival of Mars' due to its red color. This supergiant is shedding matter so efficiently that it is surrounded by a vast reflection nebula of its own dust.

name: POLLUX
intel: The brightest star in Gemini (brighter than its 'twin' Castor). In 2006, an exoplanet (Thestias) with at least 2.3 times the mass of Jupiter was confirmed orbiting this giant star.

name: FOMALHAUT
intel: Famous for its massive debris ring, essentially a scaled-up Kuiper Belt. It was one of the first systems where an exoplanet was directly imaged in visible light by Hubble.

name: DENEB
intel: The farthest first-magnitude star. It is a white supergiant, one of the most luminous stars known. If it were at the distance of Sirius, it would cast shadows on Earth.

name: MIMOSA
intel: Beta Crucis is a Beta Cephei variable, meaning it pulsates rapidly. The primary star has a solar wind blowing at 2,000 km/s, creating a shockwave in the surrounding gas.

name: REGULUS
intel: Regulus rotates so fast that if it spun 10% faster, it would fly apart. It lies almost exactly on the ecliptic, meaning the Moon frequently occults (passes in front of) it.

name: ADHERA
intel: Historically called the 'Virgins'. This star is one of the brightest Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) sources in the entire sky, capable of ionizing hydrogen gas clouds light years away.

name: SHAULA
intel: Lambda Scorpii represents the scorpion's stinger. It is a complex triple system including a Beta Cephei variable and a pre-main-sequence star that emits X-rays.

name: CASTOR
intel: To the eye, a single star. Telescopically, a binary. Spectroscopically, a sextuple system. It consists of three pairs of binary stars dancing in a complex gravitational web.

name: GACRUX
intel: The nearest M-class red giant to the Sun. Unlike the other stars in the Southern Cross which are hot blue B-types, Gacrux is a cool, old star appearing distinctly orange-red.

name: BELLATRIX
intel: Known as the 'Amazon Star'. It is a hot blue giant that was once thought to be part of the Orion Association, but is actually much closer to us than the rest of Orion's stars.

name: ELNATH
intel: A chemically peculiar star with unusually high levels of Manganese and Mercury. It sits on the border of Taurus and Auriga, often historically shared by both constellations.

name: MIAPLACIDUS
intel: An evolved giant star located in the 'Diamond Cross' asterism (not the Southern Cross). It is unusually devoid of a companion star or debris disk.

name: ALNILAM
intel: The center star of Orion's Belt. Alnilam is losing mass 20 million times faster than the Sun. Its intense UV radiation is illuminating the NGC 1990 molecular cloud around it.

name: ALNITAK
intel: The eastern star of Orion's Belt. It is a rare O-type supergiant, the hottest class of stars. It lies directly adjacent to the famous Horsehead Nebula and the Flame Nebula.

name: ALIOTH
intel: The brightest star in the Big Dipper (brightness varies slightly). It is a magnetic Ap star with strange spectral lines of Chromium and Europium separated by its magnetic field.

name: DUBHE
intel: One of the 'Pointer Stars' (with Merak) that points to Polaris. Unlike most of the Dipper stars, Dubhe is not part of the Ursa Major Moving Group but is passing through.

name: MIRFAK
intel: A yellow supergiant dominating the Alpha Persei Cluster. Binoculars reveal dozens of fainter B-type stars surrounding it, all born from the same gas cloud.

name: WEZEN
intel: One of the most luminous stars in the region. Though it appears dim due to distance, if Wezen were as close as Sirius, it would shine as bright as a half-moon.

name: SARGAS
intel: A rapidly rotating bright giant. It is evolving quickly from a blue star into a red giant. Within a few million years, it will become a Cepheid variable star.

name: KAUS AUS
intel: Known as a 'Shell Star'. It rotates so rapidly that it has flung off a disk of gas from its equator, creating unusual spectral emission lines.

name: AVIOR
intel: A rare eclipsing binary that is not variable to the naked eye. It consists of a Helium-burning orange giant and a hydrogen-fusing blue dwarf.

name: ALKAID
intel: The star at the very tip of the Big Dipper's handle. At 17,000 Kelvin, it is one of the hottest stars visible to the naked eye without a telescope.

name: MENKALINAN
intel: An eclipsing binary system. The two stars are nearly identical and are tidally locked, meaning they always show the same face to each other as they orbit.

name: ATRIA
intel: An 'Hybrid Star' with a cool stellar wind and a hot corona. It serves as a navigational anchor for the southern constellation of the Triangle.

name: ALHENA
intel: The star marking the foot of Pollux. It is a subgiant star that has just exhausted its core hydrogen. A highly eccentric asteroid belt is suspected to orbit it.

name: PEACOCK
intel: A spectroscopic binary. The primary star rotates incredibly fast, likely preparing to explode as a supernova in the distant future. It helps locate the celestial south pole.

name: ALSEPHINA
intel: One of the stars forming the 'False Cross', often confusing navigators looking for the Southern Cross. It is actually a triple system.

name: MIRZAM
intel: The 'Roarer' or 'Herald', rising just before Sirius. It is a Beta Cephei variable, its surface physically pulsating in complex rhythms every 6 hours.

name: ALPHARD
intel: The 'Solitary One', named because it sits in a very empty region of the sky. It is a Barium star, enriched with heavy elements from a now-dead white dwarf companion.

name: POLARIS
intel: The North Star. It is a Classical Cepheid variable (standard candle) and actually a triple star system. It lies less than 1 degree from the true Celestial North Pole.

name: HAMAL
intel: Historically important as the Vernal Equinox point in ancient times. In 2011, a planet with 1.8x the mass of Jupiter was confirmed orbiting this giant.

name: ALGOL
intel: The 'Demon Star'. It is the prototype of eclipsing binaries. Every 2.8 days, the dimmer star passes in front of the brighter one, causing the star to visibly 'wink' for 10 hours.

name: DIPHDA
intel: Despite being an evolved giant, it emits X-rays 2,000 times stronger than the Sun, suggesting intense magnetic activity usually only seen in young stars.

name: NUNKI
intel: The oldest star name in existence, found on Euphratean tablets. It lies extremely close to the Ecliptic, meaning planets and the Moon frequently block it from view.

name: ALPHECCA
intel: The jewel in the Northern Crown. It is an eclipsing binary similar to Ursa Major stars. A debris disk of dust orbits the pair, similar to the Sun's Kuiper Belt.

name: SCHEDAR
intel: The bottom-right star of the 'W'. It is a stable orange giant. High-resolution imaging has shown no starspots, indicating a very quiet magnetic surface.

name: ASPIDISKE
intel: A rare spectral type A supergiant. It is currently crossing the 'Instability Strip' on the HR diagram, meaning it will likely begin pulsating as a variable star soon.

name: SUHAIL
intel: An erratic variable star. It is an evolved supergiant that creates shockwaves in its outer atmosphere, fusing heavy elements in its core before an eventual supernova.

name: CAPH
intel: A Delta Scuti variable star. It rotates once every day (very fast for a giant), causing it to flatten at the poles. It is currently in the 'Hertzsprung Gap' of evolution.

name: RUCHBAH
intel: An Algol-type eclipsing binary. It emits an excess of infrared radiation, confirming the presence of a debris disk, likely from colliding asteroids.

name: SEGIN
intel: A massive blue giant at the end of the 'W'. It marks the celestial position of the Autumnal Equinox in the era of 2000-4000 AD.

name: MERAK
intel: One of the Pointers. It is a 'Vega-like' star, surrounded by a disk of warm dust that has a mass similar to Saturn, suggesting a planetary system is present.

name: PHECDA
intel: An Ae star, meaning it is surrounded by a gaseous envelope. It is rapidly rotating and is physically associated with the Mizar-Alcor system.

name: MEGREZ
intel: The dimmest star of the Big Dipper. It connects the handle to the bowl. Its faintness compared to its siblings is due to its lower mass (1.6 Solar masses).

name: MIZAR
intel: The first telescopic binary ever discovered (1617). Mizar itself is a quadruple system. When combined with Alcor, it forms a loosely bound sextuple system.

name: ALCOR
intel: The 'Rider' of the horse. Ancient armies used the ability to distinguish Alcor from Mizar as an eyesight test. It has a red dwarf companion.

name: KOCHAB
intel: Between 1500 BC and 500 AD, Kochab served as the North Star. A gas giant planet, approximately 6.1 Jupiter masses, orbits this star every 522 days.

name: PHERKAD
intel: A shell star. It has a circumstellar disk of gas created by its own rapid rotation and stellar wind. It varies slightly in brightness.

name: MINTAKA
intel: The western star of the Belt. It is a complex multiple system. The primary is an eclipsing binary where a hot O-type star and a B-type star eclipse every 5.7 days.

name: SAIPH
intel: Orion's right knee. Although it is as hot and massive as Rigel, it emits most of its energy in the ultraviolet, making it appear dimmer to the human eye.

name: GRAFFIAS
intel: A system of at least six stars. Because it lies near the ecliptic, it can be occulted by the Moon and planets. Jupiter occulted it in 1971.

name: DSCHUBBA
intel: In 2000, this star suddenly flared in brightness due to shedding a layer of gas. It is a Gamma Cassiopeiae variable, throwing off plasma disks.

name: WEI
intel: An orange giant that varies in brightness. It is an important X-ray source. It helps form the lower curve of the Scorpion's tail.

name: LESATH
intel: Located just adjacent to Shaula (the Stinger). The pair is known as the 'Cat's Eyes'. Lesath is a subgiant evolving towards the giant phase.

name: ALGIEBA
intel: A binary system resolvable with good telescopes. In 2009, a planetary companion (8.8 Jupiter masses) was discovered orbiting the primary star.

name: ZOSMA
intel: Located on the Lion's hip. It is rotating rapidly (180 km/s) and is part of the Ursa Major Moving Group, sharing a common origin with the Big Dipper.

name: ALBIREO
intel: The 'Jewel of Cygnus'. A famous double star with striking color contrast—one bright gold, the other deep blue. It is debated whether they are a true binary or an optical double.

name: SADR
intel: Located in the center of the Northern Cross. It is surrounded by the diffuse emission nebula IC 1318, which it illuminates.

name: GIENAH
intel: An orange giant in the wing of the Swan. It is a Red Clump star, meaning it is currently fusing helium in its core, a stable phase of old age.

name: MARKAB
intel: The 'Saddle' of the horse. It emits excess infrared radiation, indicating a debris disk. It will evolve into a red giant within the next few million years.

name: SCHEAT
intel: A red giant that varies irregularly in brightness. It has a very low surface gravity, allowing a strong stellar wind to blow its outer layers into space.

name: ALPHERATZ
intel: A 'Mercury-Manganese' star. Its atmosphere has distinct clouds of these heavy metals kept separate by the lack of convection currents in its atmosphere.

name: MIRACH
intel: A bright red giant used as a guide to find the Andromeda Galaxy. Just 7 arcminutes away lies NGC 404, a dwarf galaxy nicknamed 'Mirach's Ghost'.

name: ALMACH
intel: A stunning quadruple system. Through a telescope, it splits into a golden-yellow giant and a blue companion. The blue companion is itself a tight triple star.

name: MENKAR
intel: A red giant losing mass. It is a variable star that is currently burning helium into carbon. Its name means 'Nostril' in Arabic.

name: KAUS MEDIA
intel: The middle of the Archer's bow. It is an orange giant with three faint dim companions. It is part of the local Gould Belt of stars.

name: KAUS BOREALIS
intel: The top of the bow. It is an orange giant. It points almost directly towards the center of the Milky Way galaxy.

name: ALNASL
intel: The arrowhead. It produces a stellar wind like the Sun, but much stronger. It is currently moving towards the Galactic Center at 21 km/s.

name: ASCELLA
intel: A binary system with an orbital period of 21 years. The pair has a moderate eccentricity, swinging close and then far apart in their dance.

name: POLIS
intel: A massive supergiant system. The primary is eclipsed by a companion every 180 days. It lies at a tremendous distance but is still visible to the eye.

name: RUKBAT
intel: Though designated Alpha Sagittarii, it is far from the brightest star in the constellation. It is a blue dwarf surrounded by a debris disk.

name: ANCAA
intel: A spectroscopic binary. The companion orbits the main orange giant every 10.5 years. It is currently in a stable helium-fusion phase.

name: ALUDRA
intel: A massive blue supergiant in the final stages of its life. It will explode as a supernova. It is one of the most distant stars visible to the naked eye.

name: MULIPHEIN
intel: A bright giant star. It sits in the collar of the Great Dog. It is a chemically peculiar HgMn star with unusual surface abundances.

name: FURUD
intel: A spectroscopic binary. The companion is invisible to telescopes but detected by the wobble of the main star. Orbit is 675 days.

name: RASALHAGUE
intel: It spins at 88% of its breakup velocity. This extreme speed creates a gravity darkening effect, where the poles are thousands of degrees hotter than the equator.

name: CEBALRAI
intel: The 'Shepherd's Dog'. It is a variable star. Radial velocity variations suggest it may host a planetary companion.

name: SABIK
intel: A binary of two white stars. Their orbit is highly eccentric (oval-shaped), causing them to swing very close and then retreat far apart every 129 years.

name: YED PRIOR
intel: A red giant rich in Nitrogen. It is located near the celestial equator. The surface temperature is relatively cool at 3,850 Kelvin.

name: MARFIK
intel: A binary system. The name means 'The Elbow'. It is a variable star of the Algol type, meaning the stars eclipse each other.

name: ETAMIN
intel: The 'Zenith Star' of London (it passes directly overhead there). In 1.5 million years, it will be the brightest star in the sky as it passes close to Earth.

name: ALDERAMIN
intel: Because of Earth's precession, this will be the North Star around 7500 AD. It rotates very quickly for an evolved star, indicating magnetic braking has not slowed it yet.

name: ALFIRK
intel: The prototype of Beta Cephei variables. The iron content in its core causes the entire star to pulsate, changing brightness every few hours.

name: ERRAI
intel: A binary system. In 1988, it was the first system where an exoplanet was suspected, though it wasn't confirmed until 2002. The planet 'Tadmor' is 1.6 Jupiter masses.

name: TARAZED
intel: A bright giant burning helium. It is rich in Carbon-13. Even though it looks close to Altair in the sky, it is actually much further away in the background.

name: ALSHAIN
intel: A subgiant star very similar to what our Sun will look like in a few billion years. It has a faint red dwarf companion, Beta Aquilae B.

name: DENEB OKAB
intel: The 'Tail of the Eagle'. It rotates at 200 km/s. This rapid spin flattens the star into an oblate spheroid.

name: ROTANEV
intel: A binary system of two subgiants. Its name is 'Venator' spelled backwards, named after the assistant to famous astronomer Piazzi.

name: SUALOCIN
intel: A system of seven stars. Its name is 'Nicolaus' spelled backwards. It rotates fast and produces a strong stellar wind.

name: ZUBENELGENUBI
intel: A wide visual binary easily split with binoculars. The two stars are 5,000 AU apart (roughly 140 times the Pluto-Sun distance) but moving together through space.

name: ZUBENESCHAMALI
intel: Historically reported as appearing green, a very rare color for stars. Modern observers usually see it as white or pale blue. It is a rapid rotator.

name: UNUKALHAI
intel: The heart of the Serpent. It emits surprisingly strong X-rays for an old giant, suggesting active magnetic loops on its surface.

name: VINDEMIATRIX
intel: The 'Grape Gatherer'. Its morning rising once signaled the time for wine harvest. It is a high-velocity star moving rapidly through the galaxy.

name: PORRIMA
intel: A spectacular binary for telescopes. The two stars are nearly identical twins. Their orbit is highly elliptical, swinging them close together every 169 years.

name: COR CAROLI
intel: The prototype 'Alpha2 Canum Venaticorum' variable. It has an incredibly strong magnetic field (5,000x Earth's) that creates starspots of specific chemical elements.

name: IZAR
intel: Named 'Pulcherrima' (The Most Beautiful) by Struve. In a telescope, it resolves into a striking pair: a bright orange giant and a faint blue main-sequence star.

name: MUPHRID
intel: A subgiant rich in heavy elements. It appears close to Arcturus in the sky and actually lies at a similar distance, making them stellar neighbors.

name: ALKALUROPS
intel: A triple star system. The primary is a white subgiant. The secondary is actually a close pair of stars that flare in brightness due to magnetic activity.

name: NEKKAR
intel: A flare star, which is unusual for a giant. It emits bursts of X-rays. Its outer atmosphere is expanding and cooling as it ages.

name: SEGINUS
intel: A Delta Scuti variable. The star physically swells and shrinks in complex non-radial pulsation modes, changing brightness slightly every few hours.
